goal: Players open their own worlds, find other people's without any central service, link them with portals and walk between them; missing mods download on the way; identity and achievements live on Chia. The game in those worlds: survival in the Valheim spirit with real temperatures and seasons, and animals to tame, breed and raise, from real facts.

pieces.name: Living world
pieces.what: The loop: seasons bring heat and rain, rain grows plants, plants feed grazers, grazers feed hunters, and what dies goes back to the soil. Each part reads five shared things (the place, the climate table, the plant table, food categories, the forage goal) instead of rules of its own.

parts.name: Real places and pacing
parts.note: Researched (2026-11-03): a real place and its monthly climate for every biome, 57 plants' agronomy, real diets and food webs, and the pacing (the calendar for weather, the species' growing pace for plants). Decided: the fern forest after the Yixian (cool), the dunes wet in winter and spring, Velociraptors alone, temperatures as the real places have them. The climate table follows it (vitals/tests/places.rs holds it there). Next: the plant table and the species' diets.

parts.name: Rain by season
parts.note: Each biome rains on its real place's share of each season's days, in spells of a few hours (mods/base/src/weather.rs); the engine draws rain only there (set_rain, raining_at); /rain tells today's spell. Not yet: snow drawn by temperature (a taiga winter spell shows rain), the Cretaceous's wet-season label per biome.

parts.name: Soil water
parts.note: Worked out from the biome's last 8 days of rain, drying faster in the heat (vitals::plants::soil_water), so nothing is stored; ground within 4 blocks of water is soaked (base_api::ground_at).

parts.name: Plants by the place
parts.note: Wheat, berry bushes, saplings, sugar cane and cactus grow at warmth × water from their real agronomy (vitals::plants, growth.rs); wheat and berries at the growing pace (26 and 20 minutes at best), berries ripe only in summer and autumn; /growth shows the rate. Grazed grass grows back (forage). Frost kills tender crops by their real frost points (spring wheat, berries' fruit, cane and cactus stalks to the base; vitals::plants frost, growth.rs), not yet seen in the game. Not yet: the new crops and wild plants (winter wheat and rye, hardy).

parts.name: Food categories and diets
parts.note: Twelve kinds of food (vitals::food::Category) on every food item, and every species' researched diet as shares (Species::eats), shown in the sheets. Not yet: taming foods from the categories.

parts.name: Wild hunger and foraging
parts.note: Wild plant eaters get hungry; one forage goal finds tall grass (grazed short, growing back by warmth and rain), ripe berries and leaves, and eats until full (mods/animals/src/forage.rs, vitals::forage). Not yet: hunters' hunger (with prey), food off the ground, drinking.

parts.name: Food web per biome
parts.note: Researched: every biome's web is whole with 2 new full creatures and 14 simple ones in the overworld (wolf, jaguar; hare, rodent, small bird, deer, reindeer, fish, caiman, fox, coyote, eagle, owl, vulture, raven, gull), the farm animals as their wild forms, and Protoceratops, an iguanodont and 8 simple ones in the Cretaceous. Wave one: hare, rodent, deer, fish, fox, raven; Protoceratops, a small mammal, a lizard.

parts.name: New species, wave one
parts.note: The smallest set that makes hunting visible: hare, rodent, deer, fish, fox and raven; Protoceratops, a small mammal and a lizard. Simple creatures first (one model, few animations), wild only (Taming::Wild: they live, flee, breed and get eaten). Built: the hare, as two species on one model (the brown hare of open country and the mountain hare of the north, white in the snow), the wood mouse (fields, woods, the desert, the llanos, the dunes) the field vole (taiga, birch woods, tundra, mountains, marshes), and the deer as two species on one model (the white-tailed deer of the Americas and the red deer of Europe, antlers on males through a gene their sex sets), and the fish as two species on one model (the brown trout of cool rivers and lakes, the pacu of the swamp and llanos), each with coat genes, spawning in its habitats and running from hunters; their shared behaviour is mods/animals/src/wild.rs, and fish swim and come by the mod's own water spawner (mods/animals/src/fish.rs: the engine spawns nothing in water), not breeding yet; and the foxes, the first new hunters (the red fox of the north and the Arctic fox of the tundra on one model: hungry, they hunt voles, mice, hares and birds by size and eat their kill; seen taking a mouse and a hare), and the raven, the carrion bird of the cold biomes (on the ground and in the air: it takes off from walkers and hunters on its flying model and lands again; no nests yet, its young come out as fledglings); and Protoceratops, the Cretaceous's plant eater and the raptors' prey (herds on the red dunes and the scrubland, cropping ferns: the Cretaceous ferns are browse now, mods/base/vitals/src/forage.rs; eggs in nests in the wet season). and Kryptobaatar, the Cretaceous's small mammal (a multituberculate on the wood mouse's build). and the lizard, Priscagama (an early agamid: sprawling, bobbing its head and doing push-ups, basking flat). All ten are built, each seen in the game; still for later: nests for the raven, breeding for the fish. Reviewed against the blocky-model checklist (2026-11-03): the mouse, vole, Kryptobaatar, lizard and fish are painted finer (house.FINE, 256 texels a block: at 64 their heads were 2-3 texels, the eyes black squares), every one with eyes that blink, the raven's eye redrawn, Protoceratops' eyes bigger and its frill a plate.

parts.name: Hunters and prey
parts.note: Wild hunters get hungry with prey at home and hunt by their researched prey sizes (never their own family or players), a kill feeds them, prey run from hunters that can take them (mods/animals/src/hunt.rs). Seen: a chihuahua took a chicken, a wyvern a raptor, a pig and a cat. Not yet: packs taking big prey together, scavenging, hunting players (a decision).

parts.name: Capacity and populations
parts.note: Plant eaters come by natural spawning as often as their food grows this season (never under a fifth; the engine's new natural-spawn question), arrive as fed as the place feeds them, a quarter young in their breeding season, and starve to death on an empty stomach in a game day (wild only). Dry-season grass is poor fodder. Not yet: hunters' capacity, standing water in swamps.

parts.name: Death, dung and rot
parts.note: Grazers leave dung; a compost bin takes spoiled food, dung, rotten flesh and plant waste and rots it into compost (vitals::soil, farming.rs); kills' drops stay as carcasses. Not yet: food and carcasses rotting away on the ground, scavengers, the generated art.

parts.name: Fertile soil
parts.note: Farmland's fertility 3 to 0 sets crops' growth 100% to 20%; a ripe wheat harvest wears a level, dung and compost give levels back, a season unplanted one; hoes till grass and dirt (new). Not yet: clover and beans.

parts.name: Loop balance checks
parts.note: Built: animals_core::web checks every food in a diet is in the world, every plant eater eats in each habitat every season, every hunter has prey where it lives, every biome has plants, plant eaters, hunters and a carrion eater, and everything but the top hunters is prey; the species sheet shows each biome's web and the gaps the plan fills (web::WAITING, 14 now: wave two and the Cretaceous tier 2). It found winter bare, so the world gained winter hay, twigs and mast, lichen, fungi, roots, insects and water plants (vitals::forage). Every plant grows somewhere (vitals/tests/places.rs). A year holds (web::grazing): in each biome's best season its grazers' full crowds eat at most 18% of what its tall grass grows back (far under real grazers' quarter to half: a choice for later); the grass cover moved to vitals::forage::GRASS_COVER, which worldgen reads.
